# Revcenter API

> Run candidate searches, read scored profiles and build shortlists from your own systems and AI tools.

Every page is also available as Markdown: add `.md` to its address. All pages in one file: https://docs.revcenter.ai/llms-full.txt

## Get started

- [Overview](https://docs.revcenter.ai/introduction.md): Run candidate searches, read scored profiles and build shortlists from your agent, terminal or apps.
- [Quickstart](https://docs.revcenter.ai/quickstart.md): From login to a scored shortlist with the revcenter CLI, or with curl.
- [Authentication](https://docs.revcenter.ai/authentication.md): API keys, the CLI's browser login, and how to give an agent access safely.

## Concepts

- [Execution model](https://docs.revcenter.ai/concepts/execution-model.md): The primitives Revcenter runs on, what each does, and which tools expose it.
- [CLI basics](https://docs.revcenter.ai/concepts/cli-basics.md): How the revcenter CLI logs in, where it keeps the key, what it prints, and how it exits.

## Tools

- [Connectors](https://docs.revcenter.ai/tools/connectors.md): Add Revcenter to Claude and ChatGPT from the browser, or to your own LLM or agent with an API key: one URL.
- [CLI reference](https://docs.revcenter.ai/tools/cli.md): Every revcenter command, its options, and whether it uses credits.
- [MCP](https://docs.revcenter.ai/tools/mcp.md): Use Revcenter as tools in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and other MCP clients.
- [Agents](https://docs.revcenter.ai/tools/agents.md): Hand a search to an AI agent: setup, the workflow, and a prompt to start from.

## Guides

- [Writing a search](https://docs.revcenter.ai/guides/writing-a-search.md): How to ask for the people you want: what narrows who is searched, what ranks them, and tips that improve results.
- [Search approaches](https://docs.revcenter.ai/guides/search-approaches.md): The ways a request can be searched, what each one asks for before anything is spent, and when to use it.
- [Criteria](https://docs.revcenter.ai/guides/criteria.md): What a search looks for: which fields filter LinkedIn before anything is read, and which score after.
- [Searches and shortlists](https://docs.revcenter.ai/guides/searches.md): How a search runs, what its outcome means, and how to get more people without starting over.
- [Rate limits](https://docs.revcenter.ai/guides/rate-limits.md): Request and search limits, the 429 response, and how to retry.
- [Errors](https://docs.revcenter.ai/guides/errors.md): The error shape, every code the API returns, and which requests are safe to retry.
- [Pagination](https://docs.revcenter.ai/guides/pagination.md): Cursor pagination on list endpoints, page sizes, and the deprecated offset.
- [Async jobs](https://docs.revcenter.ai/guides/async-jobs.md): Searches and expansions run in the background: how to wait and which statuses mean done.
- [Webhooks](https://docs.revcenter.ai/guides/webhooks.md): Get search results delivered to your own systems as they happen: events, the signed envelope, verifying signatures in Node and Python, retries and deduplication.
- [Billing](https://docs.revcenter.ai/guides/billing.md): Credits: what a search reserves, what it is charged, and what is free.

## Recipes

- [Run a search and export the shortlist](https://docs.revcenter.ai/recipes/run-a-search.md): From criteria to a CSV shortlist with the revcenter CLI, with the output to expect at each step. Reserves up to 1,000 credits.
- [Run a search from a coding agent](https://docs.revcenter.ai/recipes/coding-agent.md): Connect Claude Code or Codex, give the agent a brief, and check what it runs. Reserves up to 1,000 credits.
- [Run a search from a backend job](https://docs.revcenter.ai/recipes/backend-job.md): A Node.js job that launches a search safely, waits for it, pages through the people and saves the shortlist CSV. Reserves up to 1,000 credits.

## Use cases

- [Executive search sourcing](https://docs.revcenter.ai/use-cases/executive-search.md): Turn a mandate into criteria, run one search, and refine the slate without spending again.
- [Shortlist delivery to clients](https://docs.revcenter.ai/use-cases/client-shortlists.md): Keep a project's shortlist current from your own systems and deliver it as a CSV or through the app.
- [Agent-driven research](https://docs.revcenter.ai/use-cases/agent-research.md): Let an AI agent draft criteria, run a search and explain the results, with you approving each spend.

## API reference

- [API reference](https://docs.revcenter.ai/api-reference/introduction.md): The Revcenter HTTP API: base URL, request and response shape.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/health: Health. Whether the API is up. No key needed. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/auth/device: Start a device login. Start a device login, for a machine with no browser. Show the person verification_uri_complete and user_code, then poll POST /auth/token every interval seconds. No key needed. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/auth/token: Finish a login. Trade a sign-in for a key, returned once. A browser sign-in sends grant_type authorization_code with the code from the loopback redirect, its PKCE code_verifier and the same redirect_uri. A device login polls with device_code: authorization_pending (or slow_down) until someone authorizes it at /oauth/device. Errors: access_denied, expired_token, invalid_grant. No key needed. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/auth/revoke: Revoke this key. The key in the Authorization header revokes itself, as revcenter auth logout does. Answers revoked: false for a key that is already revoked or unknown. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/me: Who am I. The key's workspace, name, scopes and expiry, the person it acts as and their role, the workspace's plan and limits, and today's usage. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/me/usage: Today's usage. Today's requests and searches, and credits remaining. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/capacity: Live capacity. How busy Revcenter is right now: searches running and waiting across the platform and in this workspace, and about when a search launched now would start. Launches are never refused for being busy: a search past the platform's limit waits its turn (status queued) and starts as one finishes. Workspaces take turns, so a workspace with many searches waiting does not hold up another's first one. Use this to tell the person what to expect before launching many searches at once. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/billing/top-up: Buy more credits. A Stripe checkout link to add credits to this workspace at its plan's rate; open it to pay. Nothing is charged until someone pays on that page. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/actions: List actions. Every action this API offers, with its route, scope and cost class: the catalog the MCP tools are built from. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/actions/preview: Preview an action. What an action would do and spend, without doing it; returns a proposal_id that apply_proposal runs within 30 minutes. Works for every action marked proposable in GET /actions. Previewing a requirement change re-scores nothing until it is applied, except that its before/after is computed on the people already read. Previewing launch_search with criteria returns compiled_query: the exact titles, keyword terms, locations, level, years and employers the search will send. page_one_estimate is null in a preview (reading page 1 is paid); the search records it once it runs. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/proposals/apply: Apply a proposal. Run an action previewed with preview_action, exactly as previewed. Applying the same proposal twice returns the first result. The key needs the scope of the action the proposal runs, too. Uses what its preview stated: a search or an expansion reserves up to its max_credits and refunds what it doesn't use; anything else is free.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/reference/criteria: Criteria reference. Every criteria field, whether it filters LinkedIn before anything is bought or scores after, its allowed values, and an example. Read it before launch_search. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/criteria/draft: Draft criteria from a job description. Revcenter's reading of a job description as criteria, the way the app drafts a search: review it, change what the person asks, then launch it as criteria. Launches nothing. The same reading the app's composer makes: titles and their closest synonyms, the role's own place and radius, years, and requirements as short terms, with the rest as scored context. `review.warnings` names anything to check before launching (a place wider than the role's own); `compiled_query` is the exact query the criteria will send. Pass `project_id` to check the place against the project's name too. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/reference/industries: Find industries. LinkedIn industries matching a word, with their ids; use the labels in current_industries and exclude_industries. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects: List projects. The workspace's projects, newest first, with how many searches each ran and how many are on its shortlist. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects: Create a project. Make a project: one role, one shortlist. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}: Get a project. One project, with its search and shortlist counts. Does not use credits.
- PATCH https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}: Rename or archive a project. Rename a project, or archive it (or bring it back): an archived project leaves list_projects but keeps its searches, shortlist and share link. Does not use credits.
- DELETE https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}: Delete a project. Delete a project for good, sending its exact name as confirm_name. Its shortlist, share link and do-not-contact list go with it; its searches and the people they found stay. Cannot be undone. confirm_name must be the project's name exactly as get_project returns it, or nothing is deleted (400 confirmation_required). The share link stops showing the list, so a client holding it sees nothing: to keep it, archive instead (update_project with archived true). A project with delivered work behind it is kept (409 project_in_use). Preview it with preview_action first to show the person what goes. Does not use credits. It can't be undone, so the MCP server asks the person first, naming what goes.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/insights: Project insights. The talent picture across a project's searches, as the app's Insights tab shows it: totals and verdict counts, and where the people are, who employs them, their titles, schools and skills. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/stats: Project stats. Everyone a project's searches scored, in aggregate: how many were analyzed and qualified, the score spread, how many are on the shortlist, and the most common reasons people were rejected. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/spend: Credits a project used. The credits a project's searches used: what each reserved and was charged, what is still held by searches running now, and the project's total. search_id narrows it to one search. credits_state per search: held (running; its cap is reserved), charged (finished; charged for the pages and profile reads it bought, the rest refunded; credits_breakdown shows the arithmetic), refunded (its whole reservation came back: it failed or never started), none (database only, or no plan). Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/dnc: List do-not-contact. The people this project's searches skip, newest first: the project's own do-not-contact list and the workspace-wide one. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/dnc: Add to do-not-contact. Add people to the project's do-not-contact list by LinkedIn address: its searches skip them from now on. People already on it are left as they are. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/dnc/from-search/{searchId}: Add a whole search to do-not-contact. Add everyone a search found to the project's do-not-contact list in one call, for when the client turned down the whole list. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/searches: List a project's searches. The searches a project has run, oldest first. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/records: List every record a project's searches returned. Every person any of a project's searches returned, expansions included, once each in the order returned: status rolled up across the searches (scored, known, not_read), the best score, which searches returned them, and the read profile when this workspace holds one; fields picks slices, profile=false none (the hosted connector's tool returns profiles only when fields asks). One record per person across the project (the earliest listing wins), with the same fields as list_search_records plus first_search_id (the search that listed them first) and search_ids (every search in the project that returned them). status is scored when any of the project's searches scored them, else known when this workspace already holds them, else not_read; score is the best any of the project's searches gave. For everyone across the whole workspace, use list_candidates. No contact details. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/records.csv: Download every record a project's searches returned as CSV. Every record a project's searches returned as CSV, expansions included, one row per person: the search records' columns plus first_search_id and search_ids (joined by ;); or as JSON Lines with format=jsonl. UTF-8 with a byte order mark, so Excel reads it as written. ?format=jsonl returns JSON Lines instead: one person per line with the whole read profile, lossless; for an AI agent, JSONL; CSV is for spreadsheets. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/searches: Launch a search. Start a LinkedIn search in a project, on `criteria` as sent (a `brief` in the person's own words fills what they leave unsaid), or on a `jd_text` Revcenter reads; with database_only it scores the workspace's candidates on file and uses no credits. Send an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key, project and body returns the same search; the same key on a different request returns 409 idempotency_key_reused. max_credits (250 to 20,000; absent, the workspace's most per search; held to 1,000 on a trial, to the workspace's most per search on a plan (5,000 unless its admins set another) and to the credits left, with credits_note saying so; below 250 is refused with 400 max_credits_too_low, as a smaller cap cannot buy one page of results and read it) is reserved at launch and refused with 402 shortlist_allocation_exhausted when the workspace can't cover it; when the search finishes it is charged for the results pages and profile reads it bought (on a plan 25 credits a page of up to 25 people and 2 a profile read; on a trial 50 and 5; lookups, AI screening, people already in the workspace and cached results are free), never more than max_credits, and the rest comes back (get_search credits_charged and credits_breakdown). A search that fails is refunded in full. Reserves up to max_credits credits (by default the workspace's most per search: 1,000 on a trial, 5,000 on a plan unless its admins set another); unused credits are refunded.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/searches/{searchId}: Get a search. A search's status, stage, outcome (Shortlist ready, Poor yield, No results), how many profiles it read, and the credits it reserved and, once it closes, was charged. To wait for it, use wait_for_search rather than calling this in a loop; view=status is the light read for checking often. view=status answers only the status, stage, counts, queue place and credits (no criteria, advice or credit breakdown) and stays fast while the search runs. A search takes minutes and status running is normal; a slow answer is not an error. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/searches/{searchId}/cancel: Cancel a search. Stop a running search: it buys nothing more, scores what it already read, and keeps them. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/searches/{searchId}/people: List scored people. Everyone a search scored, best first: score, fit readings, signals and whether they are on the shortlist, and the whole read profile; fields picks slices (experience, education, skills…), profile=false none. The hosted connector's tool returns profiles only when fields asks. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/searches/{searchId}/records: List every record a search returned. Every person a search's result pages listed, read or not, in the order returned: each with what became of them (scored, known, not_read), the score if scored, and the read profile when this workspace holds one; fields picks slices, profile=false none (the hosted connector's tool returns profiles only when fields asks). list_people and the shortlist hold only the people a search scored; this is everyone it found, one record per person (the page that listed them first wins). scored: read and scored in this search. known: already in this workspace from another search, so not read again. not_read: listed but never read (screened out, left for a later round, or the search stopped). candidate_id and profile are null for people this workspace has not read. A database-only search returns no records. For every search in a project at once, use list_project_records; for everyone across the workspace, list_candidates. No contact details. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/searches/{searchId}/records.csv: Download every record a search returned as CSV. Every record a search returned as CSV, one row per person in the order returned: status, score, page, name, title, company, location, LinkedIn address, summary and headline, and the read profile's experience, education and skills as text columns and as numbered columns; or as JSON Lines with format=jsonl. Columns after candidate_id: headline, about, experience_history, education, skills, certifications, languages, projects, connections, then the career as numbered columns (experience_1_title, experience_1_company, experience_1_location, experience_1_start, experience_1_end, experience_1_months, experience_1_description … experience_10_*, education_1_school, education_1_degree, education_1_field, education_1_start, education_1_end … education_5_*, total_experience_months, current_role_months). UTF-8 with a byte order mark, so Excel reads it as written. ?format=jsonl returns JSON Lines instead: one person per line with the whole read profile, lossless; for an AI agent, JSONL; CSV is for spreadsheets. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/expand: Expand or continue a search. A live LinkedIn pass for more people on the same role, skipping everyone already found; with search_id, that search continued from where it stopped. A project's passes share its credit limit. Reserves max_credits like a launch. Without search_id: a new pass on the project's first search's criteria, once it has finished. With search_id: the same search's criteria from where it stopped, when it was stopped, interrupted or used its credits and LinkedIn still has people (pages it already read are reused at no cost); a search LinkedIn ran out of is refused with 409 cannot_continue, so expand without search_id instead. A project's searches share a credit limit of three searches' worth at the workspace's per-search limit (3,000 on a trial, 15,000 on a plan at the default 5,000 per search): a cap above what the project has left is held to it, and 409 project_credit_limit is returned when less than 250 is left. One pass at a time per project (409 search_running). Send an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key returns the same pass. Reserves up to max_credits credits (by default the workspace's most per search: 1,000 on a trial, 5,000 on a plan unless its admins set another); unused credits are refunded.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/searches/{searchId}/scoring/preview: Preview a scoring change. What a cut-off or requirement change would do to the shortlist, before and after; changes nothing. Weights are a workspace setting an admin changes in Settings. A cut-off or title-rule change is counted at once. A change that re-scores everyone runs as a scoring job: the answer is its result (with job_id and status done) when it finishes within a few seconds, else 202 with job_id and status running; get_scoring_job or wait_for_scoring returns the result. Asking the same change again returns the same job. Re-scores the people already found. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/searches/{searchId}/scoring/apply: Apply a scoring change. Apply a cut-off or requirement change: a cut-off or signal_options.needs_sponsorship (sponsorship) change is recounted from the stored scores, a requirement change re-scores everyone already read, and the shortlist moves. A cut-off or title-rule change is counted at once. A change that re-scores everyone runs as a scoring job: the answer is its result (with job_id and status done) when it finishes within a few seconds, else 202 with job_id and status running; get_scoring_job or wait_for_scoring returns the result. Asking the same change again returns the same job. An apply runs once: repeating it with the same Idempotency-Key (or applying the same proposal again) returns the same job. Re-scores the people already found. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/searches/{searchId}/scoring/jobs/{jobId}: Get a scoring job. A scoring preview or apply that is still re-scoring everyone (a job_id from preview_scoring or apply_scoring): its status, and its result once status is done. status is queued, running, done or failed. result is what preview_scoring or apply_scoring would have answered; error is set when it failed, and code busy means Revcenter was busy and nothing changed: ask again. wait_seconds (0 to 25) waits for the job to finish before answering. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/searches/{searchId}/database-pass: Search your database again. Score the workspace's candidates on file against this search; those who clear the bar join the shortlist. Re-scores the people already found. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/searches/{searchId}/scoring: Why the list looks as it does. How a search's people score now: the cut-off, people per score band, how many are shortlisted, why the rest were rejected, which must-haves profiles fail to show, and the best people just under the cut-off. Read it before preview_scoring: it says whether the cut-off or a must-have is what keeps the list short. weights are the ones in force: the workspace's from Settings when an admin set them, else the search's own. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/searches/{searchId}/scoring/discard: Discard a proposed scoring change. Discard the scoring change the app's assistant proposed for a search and left pending, keeping the criteria in force; returns what was discarded, or discarded false when nothing was pending. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/searches/{searchId}/rescore: Re-score a search. Score everyone a search already read again, under the requirements in force, and move the shortlist to match: the app's Re-score everyone. For a search whose run stopped before it scored everyone it read (the profiles are bought; they only need scoring), or to bring its list up to date. Buys nothing and changes no requirement: to change the cut-off or requirements as well, use apply_scoring. Refused with 409 search_running while a pass on the search is still running. Re-scores the people already found. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/searches/{searchId}/thread: Read a search's conversation. The project's assistant conversation in the app, oldest first, and any scoring change it proposed for this search that nobody has applied yet, with what applying it would do to the shortlist. messages is what people and the project's assistant wrote in Revcenter (the latest 200), each with its role, text and the search it was about. pending_change is null unless the assistant proposed a cut-off or requirement change for this search that would move someone and that hasn't been applied or discarded; its preview counts the shortlist before and after. To make a change yourself, use preview_scoring and apply_scoring. thread_id is null when nobody has written in the project's conversation yet. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/shortlist: Get the shortlist. Everyone on the project's live shortlist, best first, with full profiles; fields picks slices (held to one answer's size), profile=false none (the hosted connector's tool returns profiles only when fields asks). Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/shortlist.csv: Download the shortlist CSV. The shortlist as CSV: score, fit readings (score_breakdown) and why, every profile field as text and as numbered columns, and the profile as JSON in the last column; or as JSON Lines with format=jsonl. Columns: rank, score, first_name, last_name, title, company, metro, linkedin_url, personal_email, open_to_work, tenure, signals, title_match, geo_fit, industry_match, skills_match, tier, reject_code, score_breakdown (each fit reading as `criterion: reading`, joined by ; ), why (the readings that matched in full, then signals), headline, shortlist_version, about, experience_history, education, skills, certifications, languages, projects, connections, the career as numbered columns (experience_1_title, experience_1_company, experience_1_location, experience_1_start, experience_1_end, experience_1_months, experience_1_description … experience_10_*, education_1_school, education_1_degree, education_1_field, education_1_start, education_1_end … education_5_*, total_experience_months, current_role_months), profile_json. UTF-8 with a byte order mark, so Excel reads it as written. ?format=jsonl returns JSON Lines instead: one person per line with the whole read profile, lossless; for an AI agent, JSONL; CSV is for spreadsheets. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/share-link: Get the share link. The project's one public shortlist link, to paste into an email to the client; it always shows the live shortlist. Every project has exactly one link, made with the project, so this returns the same URL every time and never mints a second one. Anyone with the link can open the list, and it shows the shortlist as it stands: remove anyone who shouldn't be seen before sending it, and after a change send the same link again. `shortlisted` is how many people it shows now; don't send a link with 0. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/shortlist/members: Add to the shortlist. Put people the project's searches found on its shortlist, by candidate id (from list_people). Does not use credits.
- DELETE https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/shortlist/members/{candidateId}: Remove from the shortlist. Take someone off the shortlist, with an optional reason. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/searches/{searchId}/candidates/{candidateId}/verdict: Record a verdict and notes. Record your team's verdict on someone a search found (accept, reject, maybe, or null to clear) with reason codes and private notes, e.g. "Ask about work authorization". The same judgement the candidate panel in the app records. Verdicts, reason codes and notes are private to your workspace: they never appear on the share link, the client portal, a shortlist email or any export. Each call is kept (get_candidate_verdicts reads the latest per person) and lands with review_state pending: Revcenter reviews verdicts to calibrate scoring, so recording one does not move the shortlist; to take someone off, use remove_shortlist_member. reason_codes are keys from list_decline_reasons. Send an Idempotency-Key to make a retry safe: the same key and body return the first verdict. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/searches/{searchId}/verdicts: Read verdicts and notes. The latest verdict, reason codes and private notes for each person in a search, newest first: what your team (or the client, on the portal) decided. source is team for a verdict recorded in the app or through this API, and client for the client's own Accept on the portal's live shortlist. Pass candidate_id for one person. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/decline-reasons: List decline reasons. Your workspace's decline reasons: the reason_codes a verdict takes. Ten defaults, then the ones your team added, most used first. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/decline-reasons: Add a decline reason. Add a decline reason your team can use in verdicts; returns its key. The same label again returns the one already there. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/shortlist/versions: List published shortlist versions. The shortlist versions published to the project's client, newest first: each a frozen copy of the shortlist, with its version number and how many people it holds. The client's portal shows the newest. publish_shortlist makes a version. A version that holds someone since taken off the shortlist or put on the do-not-contact list is withdrawn: the client can't open it, and it is not listed. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/shortlist/versions/{versionId}: Get a published version. One published shortlist version exactly as the client sees it: who is on it, best first, with title, company, place, LinkedIn address and why each is on it. Frozen when it was published: later changes to the shortlist show in the next version, not this one. No scores, notes or contact details: only what the client was given. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/shortlist/versions/{versionId}.csv: Download a published version as CSV. A published shortlist version as CSV, the same file the client downloads from their portal: rank, tier, name, title, company, location, LinkedIn address and why each person is on it; or as JSON Lines with format=jsonl. Columns: rank, tier, gaps, name, title, company, location, profile_url, evidence, snapshot_id, snapshot_version, snapshot_hash, canonical_shortlist_hash, generated_at. UTF-8 with a byte order mark, so Excel reads it as written. ?format=jsonl returns JSON Lines instead: one person per line, as get_shortlist_version lists them, with version_id and version. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/shortlist/publish: Publish the shortlist to the client. Publish the live shortlist as a new version the client's portal shows. It reaches the client, so it runs only from a proposal: preview_action, show the person, then apply_proposal once they agree. Calling this route directly is refused with proposal_required, and nothing is published. The version freezes who is on the shortlist when the proposal is applied, best first, with each person's name, title, company, place, LinkedIn address and why they are on it (a qualified match, or selected by the recruiter); never notes, scores' workings or removal reasons. Publishing a shortlist that hasn't changed returns the version already published. Send expected_members (how many people the person was shown, get_project's shortlisted) and a shortlist that has moved since is refused with shortlist_changed. Does not use credits. It reaches the client, so the MCP server asks the person first, showing who gets what.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/shortlist/email/preview: Preview the shortlist email. The email send_shortlist_email would send for the project's shortlist, without sending it: the client workspace, who it goes to, the subject, the text and the people it shows. Sends nothing and makes no link. In testing, as in the app: for keys made by a developer account only (shortlist_email_in_testing otherwise), and every email goes to Revcenter's test inbox (send_to) instead of the client workspace's members (intended_recipients). client_workspace_id defaults to the client portal the project is assigned to. url is the client's link when it already exists; otherwise it is null and sending makes it. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/shortlist/email/send: Email the shortlist to the client. Email the project's shortlist to a client workspace, as preview_shortlist_email showed it. It reaches the client, so it runs only from a proposal: preview_action, show the person who gets what, then apply_proposal once they agree. Calling this route directly is refused with proposal_required, and nothing is sent. confirm_workspace_name is the client workspace's name as the person saw it in preview_shortlist_email; a different name is refused with workspace_name_mismatch, so one client never gets another's list. Send expected_total (preview_shortlist_email's total) and a shortlist that has moved since is refused with shortlist_changed. In testing, as in the app: developer keys only, and it goes to Revcenter's test inbox, never the client's members. Applying the same proposal twice sends once. Does not use credits. It reaches the client, so the MCP server asks the person first, showing who gets what.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/projects/{projectId}/client-feedback: List the client's feedback. What the client said about the people on the project's shortlist, newest first: Accept and Not a fit on their portal's live list, and verdicts on a published version, with their reasons and notes. Each is recorded as the client gave it and waits for Revcenter's review (review_state pending, approved or rejected) before it changes any scoring. not_a_fit is true when the client passed on the person, which also takes them off the shortlist. given_on says where: the live shortlist, or a published version (version_id). Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/candidates: List the candidate database. Everyone any of this workspace's searches found, newest first, as the Candidates tab lists them; filter by text, project, title, company or place. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/candidates.csv: Download the candidate database CSV. The candidate database as CSV (up to 5,000 people, the same filters as list_candidates): every profile field as text and as numbered columns, and the profile as JSON in the last column; or as JSON Lines with format=jsonl. The career columns follow Languages: the career as numbered columns (experience_1_title, experience_1_company, experience_1_location, experience_1_start, experience_1_end, experience_1_months, experience_1_description … experience_10_*, education_1_school, education_1_degree, education_1_field, education_1_start, education_1_end … education_5_*, total_experience_months, current_role_months). UTF-8 with a byte order mark, so Excel reads it as written. ?format=jsonl returns JSON Lines instead: one person per line with the whole read profile, lossless; for an AI agent, JSONL; CSV is for spreadsheets. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/webhooks: List webhook endpoints. The workspace's webhook endpoints, newest first: URL, the events each receives, whether it is on, and why it was turned off. Never the signing secret. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/webhooks: Add a webhook endpoint. Add an HTTPS endpoint that receives search and shortlist events as signed POSTs, so results reach your systems without an agent running. Returns the signing secret once. Up to 10 endpoints a workspace. events defaults to every event (["*"]). The URL must be public HTTPS; private, loopback and link-local addresses are refused, and redirects are never followed. Store secret now: it is not shown again. Does not use credits.
- PATCH https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/webhooks/{webhookId}: Change a webhook endpoint. Change an endpoint's URL, events or description, or turn it off and on; turning it on again clears its failure count. Does not use credits.
- DELETE https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/webhooks/{webhookId}: Delete a webhook endpoint. Remove an endpoint and its delivery history; nothing more is sent to it. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/webhooks/{webhookId}/test: Send a test event. Send a webhook.test event to one endpoint now, signed like any other, and return the delivery with the status code your endpoint answered. Sent once and not retried. Works on an endpoint that is turned off, so you can check it before turning it back on. Does not use credits.
- GET https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/webhooks/{webhookId}/deliveries: List an endpoint's deliveries. What was sent to an endpoint, newest first: each event, its status (pending, delivered, failed, abandoned), attempts, the status code your endpoint answered, and when the next retry is. Does not use credits.
- POST https://api.revcenter.ai/v1/webhooks/deliveries/{deliveryId}/redeliver: Redeliver an event. Send a delivery's event to its endpoint again, now, with the same event id; retried on failure like any delivery. Does not use credits.
- [OpenAPI document](https://docs.revcenter.ai/openapi.json): the whole API, machine-readable
